sections.title: Mental model — walk the subset lattice cheaply

blocks.label: descending-submask iterator (memorize)
blocks.py:
s = mask
while s:                    # all NON-EMPTY submasks descending
    use(s)
    s = (s - 1) & mask
# total over all masks = 3^n not 4^n

blocks.md: **Superset twin:** t=(t+mask)&~mask ascending. Both directions appear in SOS/convolution problems.

options: -- leaves mask's off-bits wandering outside lattice

blocks.label: range-xor + pair hunts
blocks.py:
pre = [0]
for x in a: pre.append(pre[-1] ^ x)
def range_xor(l, r): return pre[r+1] ^ pre[l]
# count pairs xor==k: freq[pre]^k lookups per index

blocks.label: gems worth memorizing
blocks.code:
int mx = a ^ ((a ^ b) & -(a < b));      // max without branch
ll avg = (a & b) + ((a ^ b) >> 1);      // no-overflow average
x %= M_pow2  ⇔  x & (M_pow2 - 1);       // index masking
abs(x): m = x >> 31; (x ^ m) - m;       // sign-mask trick (careful INT_MIN)
swap nibbles: x = ((x & 0x0F) << 4) | ((x >> 4) & 0x0F);
blocks.py:
mx = b if a < b else a                        # branchless-ish via conditional expression
avg = (a & b) + ((a ^ b) >> 1)                 # overflow-free average
idx_masked = x & (M - 1)                       # power-of-two modulus
ax = abs(x)                                    # builtin handles INT_MIN safely

chain.a: Compilers often emit cmov anyway; branchless wins on unpredictable branches. Benchmark before bragging — say 'measured' not 'believed'.
for each bit i: for each mask with bit set: f[mask] += f[mask^(1<<i)] — accumulates sums-over-subsets in Θ(n·2ⁿ). Unlocks 'count pairs AND=0' class instantly.
Max-XOR-pair queries insert binary paths greedily matching opposite bits — flagship of Tries module; prefix-xor reduces subarray version to pair version.
Foundations L4: dense boolean universes, dp|=dp<<w shifts, /64 throughput. Combine with submask walks when both apply.
